snippet.title: Kamikaze: Japan's Suicide Pilots #ww2
snippet.description:
Being first introduced at the Battle of Leyte Gulf, these Kamikaze attacks would prove to be extremely difficult to stop, with the entire plane, not just a portion of it having to be struck and destroyed by antiaircraft fire, giving the planes that hit their target an extremely high success rate, with only 1 Japanese pilot sacrificed for every 10 American casualties.

Although only a few of these Kamakize planes would actually hit their target, with others missing their targets and falling into the ocean,  the ones that did hit were so devastating to the us fleet, that Japanese high command believed their use was worth the price… 

As a result, these attacks came to play a greater and greater role as the war progressed, with over 3,000 Kamikaze pilots sacrificing their lives during the conflict. For the Japanese, it would be their willingness to sacrifice their own lives in service to their emperor, nation, and ancestors, that they believed would bring about victory and help prevent an American invasion of the home islands.

snippet.title: The Rise and Fall of the Roman Empire
snippet.description:

snippet.title: The First Recorded Battle Ever Fought
snippet.description:
The First Recorded Battle Ever Fought. Over 3,500 years ago, armies gathered near the ancient city of Megiddo in what is now northern Israel. It was here that Pharaoh Thutmose III of Egypt confronted a coalition of Canaanite rulers in what historians consider the first battle in history to be recorded in detail.

Unlike earlier conflicts lost to time, this campaign was carefully carved into the walls of the temple of Amun at Karnak. Egyptian scribes described the march of the army, the dangerous mountain pass chosen by the pharaoh, the chaos of the battlefield, and the long siege that followed.

In this video we explore the campaign step by step, from Egypt’s march out of Gaza to the moment the gates of Megiddo finally opened after months of siege.

In this video we explore the campaign step by step, from Egypt’s march out of Gaza to the moment the gates of Megiddo finally opened after months of siege.
